the synergistic relationship among structures and processes creates a hospitable environment for interdisciplinary research, and that structures and processes are equally important in the development of interdisciplinary teams.
the structures and processes that support integration are essential to the successful integration of the social sciences in the conservation sciences.
structures and processes are important to the integration and mainstreaming of the social sciences in interdisciplinary research.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structures and processes required to integrate social science research into conservation.
the structures and processes of interdisciplinarians in the conservation sciences and the ways in which these factors influence the success of integration.
how structures and processes facilitate interdisciplinary research and, in particular, how the social sciences are integrated into conservation research and practice.

“the structures and processes that Bennett et al. propose for conservation science and practice are a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for integration and mainstreaming the social sciences.”
the framework proposed by Bennett et al. is a good first step in the right direction.
the social sciences have been integrated into conservation, but not in a way that will allow for the development of a robust and sustainable conservation science and practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is important to understand the role of structures and processes in integration.
we have developed an approach to integrate the social science into conservation that is grounded in a structure and process.

we are developing a framework for a collaborative and interdisciplinay team science that will help conservation scientists to work more effectively with social scientists to address conservation challenges.
